Where does emergency care
need a closer look?

A decision-support dashboard for state health agencies and hospital administrators to identify hospitals and regions that may need additional emergency care resources.

THE PLANNING QUESTION

ED stay times vary across hospitals. Use this evidence to focus patient-flow reviews, investigate access barriers, and prioritize local follow-up.

Understand the measures ↗
i

Time in the ED includes the whole visit. OP-18 measures arrival to departure, including care and treatment. It does not measure time until a clinician first sees a patient.

Know what is behind the numbers

DATA COLLECTION

Hospital-reported, publicly available

CMS publishes provider-level quality measures through its Provider Data Catalog. Hospitals submit data through quality reporting programs; records may be based on samples or shorter reporting periods.

This site reads the supplied Timely_and_Effective_Care-Hospital.csv from the homework folder. The original download date and release date were not supplied. We processed this snapshot on September 21, 2026; dates shown in the dashboard come from the file, not the current online release.

Preparation: retain six emergency-care measures; join on the text Facility ID; verify one record per hospital and measure; preserve reported values, sample fields, and footnotes. “Not Available” becomes missing, never zero. No patient-level data or imputation is used.

DEFINITIONS & UNITS

Compare like with like

OP-18a / b / c / d · minutes
Each value is a hospital median ED stay. The four populations are all discharged patients, general patients excluding mental health and transfers, mental health patients, and transfers. Collection: Oct 1, 2024–Sep 30, 2025.
OP-22 · percent
Patients who left before being seen. Collection: Jan 1–Dec 31, 2024. Zero is a valid reported value.
EDV · ordered category
CMS labels: low, medium, high, very high, or unavailable. Collection: Jan 1–Dec 31, 2024. The sample field is not annual ED volume.
Dashboard & state summaries
Unweighted median across reporting hospitals. Quartiles use linear interpolation at (n−1) × p. Every hospital counts equally; these are not pooled patient statistics or official CMS state averages.
Comparison benchmark
The all-location median for the same measure in this CSV; includes DC and reporting territories. It remains fixed when filters change. No clinical target is implied.
CMS measure definitions ↗CMS data dictionary ↗

Missing data, bias & uncertainty

Reporting is incomplete

Missing results may reflect small samples, non-reporting, program participation, or inapplicability. They do not establish good performance or absence of an ED. Use the “Only missing results” table control to investigate.

Hospitals are not interchangeable

Case mix, acuity, transfer roles, mental health needs, sampling, and hospital size differ. These comparisons do not adjust for those differences. Some numeric results cover a shorter period (CMS footnote 3).

State medians may hide local inequities and exclude non-reporters. Small groups are especially unstable; the dashboard always shows hospital counts.

A snapshot cannot establish a cause

The CSV provides no confidence intervals or patient-level distribution; no significance claims are made. One reporting window cannot establish persistent delays or trends. EDV and OP-18 periods differ.

Staffing, beds, transport, access distance, and real-time waits are absent. Confirm causes with local records before staffing decisions. These data are not for choosing care in an emergency.
